summary: The Iran ceasefire collapsed this week after U.S. strikes on Iranian targets, sending crude oil sharply higher and rattling bonds via renewed inflation risk. Stocks held up through rotation into energy and defensives, but duration assets sold off. Fed Chair Warsh's data-dependent stance with no forward guidance keeps real rates elevated, weighing on gold and bonds.
tweet: Iran ceasefire over, crude surging, bonds selling off — stocks hold via rotation but Warsh's no-guidance Fed keeps real rates high and gold on defense.
